Trying to hit an egg standing up at 300 yards is extremely difficult. Using a 22LR is almost impossible past 100 yards. Combine the two together and that makes this one hell of a shot.

Let me put it into context. The 22LR is a very light weight round with almost no power behind it (40 grains at 1200fps = 104 ft lb of force). The other round in the photo is a .223 (or 5.56). This is the same diameter bullet but it has a lot more power (55 grains at 3240fps = 1280 ft lb of force). The .22LR will also loose it's velocity far quicker than the 223, making it that much more difficult at greater distances.

Shooting rifles is all about stability, and standing unsupported is the most unstable position you can shoot from. Any decent marksmen can make that shot with their choice of caliber from a prone position (laying down) with how many shots she took.
